body:
## The defect

`lsms_library/country.py:640` excludes `CONTENTS.org` from the `*.org` files
folded into the cache hash, with an explicit and correct rationale:

```python
# Build-input file suffixes ... We hash *all* ``*.org`` in the relevant ``_/``
# dir except the ones below, which are pure documentation never read by a
# build step -- hashing them would cause a spurious full-country rebuild on a
# docs edit.
_ORG_HASH_SKIP = {"CONTENTS.org"}
```

The premise is false for exactly one country. `Tanzania/_/food_acquired.py:34`
reads a live build table out of it:

```python
fl = df_from_orgfile('CONTENTS.org','food_labels')
```

So editing Tanzania's `food_labels` table changes what `food_acquired` is built
from and moves **no** cache hash. The stale parquet is served, indefinitely, and
`lsms-library cache clear` is the only way to notice.

## Instances

| country | wave(s) | table | count | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tanzania | all | `food_acquired` (country-level `_/food_acquired.py`) | 1 country -- and it is the only one; `grep -rn "'CONTENTS.org'" lsms_library/countries/*/_/*.py` was run over the whole corpus | `lsms_library/countries/Tanzania/_/food_acquired.py:34` vs `lsms_library/country.py:640` |

## Why it matters

This is the same class as #757 (a `categorical_mapping.org` edit invisible to
`Wave._input_hash`) and #790 (a gitignored generated `.csv` that *is* hashed): a
build input outside the fingerprint means a correct edit produces no rebuild, and
the library then re-stamps the stale output as fresh. It is worse than a plain
staleness bug because the exclusion is *deliberate and documented* -- the next
person to read `_ORG_HASH_SKIP` will conclude, correctly for 39 countries and
incorrectly for Tanzania, that `CONTENTS.org` is documentation.

## Proposed fix

Move `food_labels` out of `Tanzania/_/CONTENTS.org` and into `_/food_items.org`,
which **is** hashed. That keeps `_ORG_HASH_SKIP`'s premise true rather than
special-casing it, and leaves `CONTENTS.org` as the documentation file every other
country's tooling assumes it is.

Cost, stated: the move forces a corpus-wide rebuild of Tanzania `food_acquired`
(the hash changes by construction). Worth scheduling with the `new_harmonize_units`
truncation fix filed alongside this one, since that rebuilds the same table.

An alternative -- narrowing `_ORG_HASH_SKIP` to a per-country setting -- would
work but leaves the trap in place for the next script that reaches into
`CONTENTS.org`.

Surfaced by the five-source price comparison, 2026-09-08; per-country evidence in `slurm_logs/price_sources/Tanzania/REPORT.org`; pattern `P20-cache-hash-hole` in `slurm_logs/price_sources/DATA_PROBLEMS.csv`.

comments.body: PR #1026 (`fix/836-tanzania-labels`, `cbc8b95a9`) resolves this issue (`Closes #836`, fires on release): the dead reader is deleted and a test guards the `_ORG_HASH_SKIP` invariant. The make-backend routing gap it exposed (no country rule, no fallback to the wave parquets) is split out as #1039.

title: Tanzania/_/food_acquired.py reads a build table out of CONTENTS.org, which the cache hash deliberately skips
